steps.title: Open the Data Manager
steps.narration: We start on the Data Manager, the page that tracks every backfill and refresh job that keeps the site's market data up to date.
steps.point_out: The 'Start a fetch / backfill job' panel, and a summary of the most recent job the site has run.

steps.title: Choose a date to refresh
steps.narration: We ask it to refresh a single day, 2015-06-18, so we can watch a job run from start to finish.
steps.point_out: The Start date field now shows the chosen date.

steps.title: Set the end of the range
steps.narration: The end date is the same day, so this is a small, quick job.
steps.point_out: The End date field now shows the chosen date.

steps.title: Start the job — and watch the ingest-time warm-up
steps.narration: Clicking Start kicks off the backfill. When it finishes, the summary line now also lists 'drawdown expectations' — a background calculation that used to wait until someone opened the Evidence page, but now runs automatically as part of the job itself.
steps.point_out: The 'Refreshed:' line growing to include 'drawdown expectations' once the job completes.

steps.title: Open Evidence right after the job — instantly
steps.narration: We open the Evidence ledger, the page that lists every certified trading claim and its historical drawdown expectations. Because the warm-up already ran during the job, this very first view loads just as fast as any later one.
steps.point_out: The claim cards and their 'Historical drawdown & dry-spell expectations' tables appearing right away, with no long spinner.

steps.title: Refresh Evidence — same numbers, still fast
steps.narration: Reloading the page shows the exact same figures. The only thing that changed this iteration is how quickly the first view loads — never the numbers themselves.
steps.point_out: Every claim's verdict, hypothesis, and expectations table look identical to before the reload.

steps.title: Confirm it in Run History too
steps.narration: Back on the Data Manager, the job we just ran shows up in Run History with the same 'drawdown expectations' note — the same background pre-computation, visible from every place this page reports on a job.
steps.point_out: The Run history row for 2015-06-18 → 2015-06-18, with 'drawdown expectations' in its small gray Refreshed note.
